usual_baseline: Around half of items met. CRAMS criteria met in 52.9% of entries [3437]. Emergency bleep documentation 44% [3331]. Most ward review questions below 80%; responsible clinician recorded in 23.3% [3277]. Personal care in nursing notes 17% [3116]. Resuscitation status 39% and capacity 14% [3225].
fix_that_works: Automating or embedding fields. Auto-filled responsible clinician rose from 23.3% to 99.5% [3277]. An electronic bleep checklist took documentation from 44% to 90% [3331]. A note format emailed with one-to-one follow-up took personal care from 17% to 89% [3116]. Discussion at daily huddles raised CRAMS compliance from 52.9% to 71.6% [3437].
fix_that_fails: Non-automated measures (teaching, posters) had limited effect; 17 questions stayed low [3277]. Resuscitation status stayed at 40–50% despite an electronic checklist [3225]. Medical ward doctor documentation only reached 57% [3331]. Many entries still missed full CRAMS criteria [3437].
consultant_advice: Generic note audits find the same thing and are hard to act on. Pick one item that matters and is missing, such as resuscitation status or capacity, and fix it in the electronic record. Mandatory or auto-completed fields beat teaching.
